newsitem.title: USA: PNC Bank Q2 net led by fee-based businesses.
newsitem.headline: PNC Bank Q2 net led by fee-based businesses.

text.p: PNC Bank Corp said strong growth in fee-based businesses boosted its second-quarter 1997 earnings.

"Our second-quarter results reflect a 21 percent increase in fee-based revenue led by growth in asset management, private banking, treasury management and capital markets," Thomas O'Brien, chairman and chief executive, said in a statement. "These businesses are among the growth opportunities we have been pursuing for some time that are now making a more meaningful contribution to our financial performance."
Non-interest income in the second quarter rose to $433.4 million from 336.6 million a year ago, an increase of 29 percent.

PNC said asset management fees increase $22 million or 17 percent primarily due to higher investment advisory, private banking and mutual fund servicing revenue. Managed assets rose to about $122 billion at the end of the quarter from $104 billion a year ago. Service fees increased $43 million or 33 percent primarily from growth in credit card, deposit and treasury management services and capital markets fee income.

PNC said taxable-equivalent net interest income for the second quarter of 1997 was $620.6 million, little changed from $619.9 million a year ago. The net interest margin widened to 3.84 percent from 3.72 percent. Average earning assets declined to $64.2 billion from $66.4 billion, reflecting a continued reduction of the securities portfolio which was offset by loan growth. PNC benefited from a higher-yielding earning asset mix. Compared with the first quarter of 1997, net interest income declined $17 million and net the interest margin fell 14 basis points.

PNC said asset quality remained strong. Nonperforming assets declined to $442 million at June 30, 1997, compared with $509 million at June 30, 1996. The ratio of nonperforming assets to total loans and foreclosed assets was 0.83 percent at June 30, 1997, and 1.03 percent a year ago.
Overall, net income rose to $259 million in the second quarter of 1997 from $248 million in the year-earlier period.
Fully-diluted earnings per share rose to $0.81 from $0.72, an increase of 13 percent.
